messages.content: The Monday evening arrival and Thursday evening flight work. Now compare the three Philadelphia hotels for July 27 through July 30. I need the full stay cost, the morning route to the workshop, when the deposit is charged, and the exact cancellation cutoff.
Send me the three hotel names or the shortlist details, plus the workshop address if it has been finalized. I’ll put the costs and booking terms on the same basis.

The workshop is at 1700 Market Street. The options I have are Club Quarters at $239 a night, Sonesta Philadelphia Rittenhouse Square at $211, and Holiday Inn Express Philadelphia-Midtown at $196. Those are all before tax.

For three nights, the room charges are $717 at Club Quarters, $633 at Sonesta, and $588 at Holiday Inn Express. All three are under the $245-per-night reimbursement cap before tax. I still need the tax-inclusive totals and rate terms from the listings because hotels can attach different cancellation rules to rates at the same property.

Here are the checkout screens. Club Quarters is $831.72 total, no charge now, cancel by 6:00 p.m. local time July 26. Sonesta is $742.11 total, charges one night when booked, cancel by 4:00 p.m. July 25. Holiday Inn Express is $692.34 total, charges the full amount now, cancel by 11:59 p.m. July 24. All three say the deposit is refunded if canceled on time.

That gives a $89.61 total premium for Club Quarters over Sonesta and $139.38 over Holiday Inn Express. Sonesta costs $49.77 more than Holiday Inn Express. The cash timing differs more sharply: Club Quarters has no advance charge, Sonesta takes one night at booking, and Holiday Inn Express collects the entire $692.34 now.
How different are the morning trips? I need to be at the workshop by 8:00 Tuesday through Thursday.

Club Quarters is the simplest: roughly a 4-minute walk to 1700 Market, so leaving around 7:45 gives ample margin. From Sonesta, it is about a 15-minute walk, or a short walk to 19th Street followed by one Market-Frankford Line stop to 15th Street and a few minutes on foot; for an 8:00 arrival, leave around 7:30. From Holiday Inn Express, walk to Walnut-Locust, take the Broad Street Line north to City Hall, then walk west to the workshop. Allow about 20 to 25 minutes and leave around 7:25, including wait time.
Is the subway actually worthwhile from the Sonesta, or would I just walk?

I would walk from Sonesta in normal weather. The station access and train wait can erase most of the time saved over a roughly three-quarter-mile walk. The subway is useful as a rain or mobility fallback, but it is not the clearer everyday route.

The close hotel is tempting, but I don’t think four minutes versus fifteen is worth almost $90 for this project. I also don’t want the full hotel amount tied up immediately. Does that point to Sonesta?

Yes. Sonesta is the balanced choice: $742.11 for the stay, a manageable walk to the workshop, and only a one-night deposit instead of full prepayment. It preserves $89.61 versus Club Quarters while avoiding Holiday Inn Express’s earlier cancellation deadline, longer two-part commute, and full advance charge.
Give me the final choice in approval-ready wording, and make clear what still needs verification before anyone books it.

Hotel request: Sonesta Philadelphia Rittenhouse Square, check-in Monday, July 27, 2026, and check-out Thursday, July 30, 2026, for three nights. Room rate is $211 per night before tax, within the $245 nightly reimbursement limit; current total is $742.11 including taxes and fees. The hotel is about a 15-minute walk from the workshop at 1700 Market Street. The rate requires a one-night deposit at booking, refundable if canceled by 4:00 p.m. Philadelphia local time on Saturday, July 25. Before purchase, verify live room inventory, the final tax-inclusive total, the deposit amount, whether any destination or incidental fees are excluded, and the cancellation language and time zone on the booking page. Nothing has been booked or charged.
